selection_contract.change_set: artifact paths changed by one eligible first-parent commit and still present in the frozen-head artifact universe
selection_contract.native_dependency_closure: changed artifacts plus every frozen-head reverse-transitive dependent under parsed domain-native import/include syntax
selection_contract.selective_revalidation: same exact reverse-transitive closure; equivalence to native closure is expected and must be retained
selection_contract.full_reset: every artifact in the frozen-head domain universe
selection_contract.gold: native dependency closure under the same frozen graph
selection_contract.gold_independence_boundary: gold and SELECTIVE_REVALIDATION use the same reachability predicate; safety is conformance, not independent semantic validation

datasets.dependency_rule: Nextflow include/from and includeConfig relative paths at the frozen head
Lean import declarations at the frozen head
ontology import declarations resolvable to frozen-head repository paths

sampling.eligible: commit has at least one changed path in the frozen-head artifact universe
sampling.take: first 100 eligible commits in reverse chronological order

statistics.interpretation: deterministic block-resampling sensitivity analysis only; no stochastic coverage guarantee

non_bypass_boundaries: The study replays public change sets against dependency syntax parsed by ORION at the frozen head; it is not a historical native build/test or native-tool replay.
Deleted paths and dependencies not representable in the frozen-head graph are outside the estimand.
Native-closure equivalence is implementation conformance, not evidence that the selector is scientifically novel or more precise than native systems.
Public Git history does not create independent adjudication, protected custody, or semantic target-obligation confirmation.
The protocol closes no issue box until a later unchanged clean-main execution passes and is reviewed.
